findings.summary: Statement catch clauses and promise rejection callbacks build the caught Error through one helper that pins the native message once, instead of two hand-rolled copies of the same value.
The catch header and the values its parameter receives are decided in one place for the immediate catch and the then rejection path, so a reporter-only parameter still lowers to catch (...) on both.
The bound rejection callback is compiled through the existing value-passing callback compiler rather than a bespoke parameter binding.
The erased-binding probe takes any identifier and body and is exposed through the lowering services, so every catch shape asks the same question instead of a statement-only one.

One native fixture covers the catch binding, the then rejection binding and the early-return shape, driven by a runtime flag so the fulfilled branch stays reachable under /W4 /WX; the feature rows state the contract in one sentence.
